question.problem:
Consider the homogeneous system ${x}^{′}(t)=Ax(t),$ where $A$ is a constant square matrix. You're given that the standard fundamental matrix ${Φ}_{0}(t)$ is the unique solution to the initial value problem

$$
{Φ}_{0}^{′}(t)=A{Φ}_{0}(t),\,{Φ}_{0}(0)={I}_{n}.
$$

A derivation of the formula for the solution $x(t)$ passing through $x({t}_{0})$ is presented below. 

$\text{L1}:\,$ Let ${Φ}_{0}(t)={e}^{At}$

$\text{L2}:\,$ $x(t)={Φ}_{0}(t)\,c$ for some constant vector $c$

$\text{L3}:\,$ $x(t)={e}^{At}\,c$ 

$\text{L4}:\,$ $x({t}_{0})={e}^{A{t}_{0}}\,c$

$\text{L5}:\,$ $({e}^{A{t}_{0}})^{-1}x({t}_{0})=({e}^{A{t}_{0}})^{-1}{e}^{A{t}_{0}}\,c$

$\text{L6}:\,$ $c={e}^{-A{t}_{0}}x({t}_{0})\,$

$\text{L7}:\,$ $x(t)={e}^{At}{e}^{-A{t}_{0}}x({t}_{0})\,$

$\text{L8}:\,$ $x(t)={e}^{At-A{t}_{0}}x({t}_{0})\,$

$\text{L9}:\,$ $x(t)={e}^{A(t-{t}_{0})}x({t}_{0})\,$

Select the correct options to justify each step of the reasoning.

$\,$ Line $\text{L6}$ follows from $\text{L5}$ by the fact that {{field-1}}.

$\,$ Line $\text{L7}$ can be obtained by {{field-2}}.

$\,$ Line $\text{L9}$ follows from $\text{L8}$ by the fact that {{field-3}}.
question.worked_solution:
Let's justify each of the selected steps.

- We first consider lines $\text{L5}$ and $\text{L6}.$ Line $\text{L5}$ gives

$$
({e}^{A{t}_{0}})^{-1}x({t}_{0})=({e}^{A{t}_{0}})^{-1}{e}^{A{t}_{0}}\,c.
$$

Since $({e}^{A{t}_{0}})^{-1}{e}^{A{t}_{0}}={I}_{n}$, the right-hand side simplifies to $c$, so

$$
c=({e}^{A{t}_{0}})^{-1}x({t}_{0}).
$$

Simplify once, then apply $({e}^{A{t}_{0}})^{-1}={e}^{-A{t}_{0}}$, to obtain

$$
c={e}^{-A{t}_{0}}x({t}_{0}),
$$

which is line $\text{L6}.$ Therefore, $\text{L6}$ follows from $\text{L5}$ by the fact that $({e}^{A{t}_{0}})^{-1}={e}^{-A{t}_{0}}.$

- Next, we consider line $\text{L7}.$ Using line $\text{L3}$ we have

$$
x(t)={e}^{At}\,c.
$$

From line $\text{L6}$, we know that $c={e}^{-A{t}_{0}}x({t}_{0}).$ Substituting this expression for $c$ into the formula for $x(t)$ gives

$$
x(t)={e}^{At}{e}^{-A{t}_{0}}x({t}_{0}),
$$

which is line $\text{L7}.$ Thus, line $\text{L7}$ can be obtained by $\text{substituting }c={e}^{-A{t}_{0}}x({t}_{0})\text{ into }x(t)={e}^{At}c.$

- Finally, we consider lines $\text{L8}$ and $\text{L9}.$ Starting from $\text{L8},$

$$
x(t)={e}^{At-A{t}_{0}}x({t}_{0}),
$$

we rewrite the exponent using the algebraic identity $At-A{t}_{0}=A(t-{t}_{0})$ to get

$$
x(t)={e}^{A(t-{t}_{0})}x({t}_{0}),
$$

which is line $\text{L9}.$ Thus, $\text{L9}$ follows from $\text{L8}$ by the fact that $At-A{t}_{0}=A(t-{t}_{0})\text{ for any }t\text{ and }{t}_{0}.$
